text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high error rate on routing-policy-cap-tier-v2 -> hosted->dedicated spillover. Spike started ~1938765400. Multiple tenants seeing 502/503 from dedicated pools. Paging primary oncall. /severity:sev2

Alex (oncall): I'm on it, taking pager. Any initial customer list?

Samir CS: seeing support tickets from two enterprise customers complaining about timeouts and model mismatches (responses truncated). CS ticket ids: CS-8921, CS-8928. They report requests that should hit hosted small models are routed to dedicated xlarge and failing.

Liz SRE: looking at routing logs. Early signal shows policy-cap-tier-v2 recently rolled at 1938762000 and has a missing evaluation clause for tenant metadata tag. It matches fallback group incorrectly.

Jordan Infra: I can throttle the spillover at the router layer if we need breathing room. Suggest set policy to fail-closed to hosted rather than escalate to dedicated.

Alex (oncall): Liz, can you paste the rule snippet? If it's a rollforward bug we should rollback to previous policy ASAP.

Liz SRE: snippet below (policy engine uses CEL-ish conditions):

```
match: request.annotations['capacity_tier'] == 'dedicated' || request.metadata.get('sla', 'standard') == 'enterprise'
actions:
  - route: dedicated-pool
  - fallback: region-fallback
```

Issue: this policy treats missing annotations as defaulting to 'enterprise' upstream via the metadata accessor; should have been explicit check for tag existence. That means some hosted traffic without explicit capacity_tier ended up matching.

Rachael Runtime: also seeing wrong model variant assignment in the dedicated pools: hosts are being assigned model variant 'xlarge-v2' instead of 'small-v1' because the variant selector relies on the capacity_tier match. So it's a double-whammy.

Maria PM: estimated customer impact? who is affected and is data path exposed?

Samir CS: two paying customers with heavy traffic are affected; internal monitoring shows ~12% of total requests in region us-west-2 hitting the misroute window, elevated 5xx rate from 0.3% -> 7% for them. No data exfil indicated, just degraded responses and timeouts.

Alex (oncall): OK plan: 1) rollback policy-cap-tier-v2 to cap-tier-v1 2) set router fallback to hosted-only for 30m 3) scale dedicated-pool down for safety 4) notify affected customers with ETA 5) run verification to confirm traffic flows back. Who can run the rollback?

Jordan Infra: I can run rollback now. Command I'll run: 
```
redwoodctl routing policy rollback --policy-id=cap-tier-v2 --to=cap-tier-v1 --region=us-west-2
```
I'll leave a hold on auto-rollouts.

Liz SRE: Before Jordan runs, add a temporary guard that changes evaluation semantics to require explicit tags: 

```
redwoodctl routing policy update --policy-id=cap-tier-v2 --set "match=has(request.annotations['capacity_tier']) && request.annotations['capacity_tier']=='dedicated'"
```
That buys time if rollback has downstream side effects.

Jordan Infra: rolling back now. Output: 

```
> rolling back policy cap-tier-v2 -> cap-tier-v1
> region us-west-2: success
> active revision: cap-tier-v1 (rev-12)
```

Incident Bot: :information_source: Policy rollback executed by Jordan Infra at 1938765575. Observability: routing error rate dropping.

Rachael Runtime: verifying variant assignments -- streaming a small sample: 

```
sample request ids: [rq-13021, rq-13022, rq-13023]
pre-rollback: routed to dedicated/xlarge-v2 -> 503
post-rollback: routed to hosted/small-v1 -> 200
```
Looks good on functional checks.

Alex (oncall): Good. Next step scale dedicated pool down to avoid further queuing. Jordan can you temporarily remove auto-scaling from dedicated-pool us-west-2?

Jordan Infra: done: 

```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool=dedicated-usw2 --min=0 --max=2 --suspend-autoscale
> success
```

Samir CS: I've drafted a customer message for the two affected customers. Basic text: "We've observed routing configuration issue that caused some requests for smaller models to route to dedicated capacity; we rolled back the policy and confirmed responses are healthy. No data exposure; we're investigating root cause and will update with a postmortem." Want approvals before sending.

Maria PM: please send to me and Alex for quick sign-off. Include the incident id and approximate window 1938765400-1938765600.

Alex (oncall): Sent to me, looks fine. Send now.

Samir CS: message sent to both customers and CS updated tickets. They acknowledged, asking for ETA on postmortem.

Rachael Runtime: monitoring showing error rate back to baseline in us-west-2 within 120s of rollback. Also verified model quality checks for a sample of 100 requests — pass.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: RESOLVED: routing-policy-cap-tier-v2 spillover mitigated. Final status: rollback to cap-tier-v1, autoscale suspended on dedicated pool, customer notifications sent. Duration ~6m.

Liz SRE: leaving notes: followup items for postmortem: 1) make metadata accessor explicit (no silent defaults) 2) add canary to policy rollouts for first 5m at 1% traffic 3) add metric alert for model-variant assignment mismatches 4) run a tabletop on routing fallbacks.

Alex (oncall): I'll own postmortem and timeline. Assigning follow-ups to Liz, Jordan, Rachael, and Samir. I'll close the incident thread after we confirm CS replies. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
